headline: Utilization-balanced allocation lands in generic_expand and collapses per-fact spread 12.0x -> 1.00x on kanto (relation cov 0.7668 -> 0.5865) at a 7.7% diversity cost. It CANNOT move EDC's cov 2.32: EDC's hydrated layer is 100% Rust festival-factory, not generic_expand/generic_synth.

premise_correction.brief_said: Implement utilization-aware sampling in generic_expand + generic_synth … report the audit `balance` cov before/after on EDC's real corpus (target cov <= 1.0 without touching the gate).
premise_correction.finding: Those two generators produce ZERO of EDC's surfaces. All 666198 EDC hydrated surfaces carry Rust festival-factory forms (declarative 90194, conversational 78474, qa_direct 52818, persona_firsttimer 43418, countdown 39620, persona_planner 38098, social_post 37916, persona_veteran 37038) and live in a single relations.jsonl per unit. EDC's hydrate stage is scripts/rehydrate_vc1.sh driving the festival-factory binary.
premise_correction.consequence: No change to generic_expand or generic_synth can alter EDC's balance cov. Reaching cov <= 1.0 on EDC requires re-hydration through the Rust generator (full-corpus provider spend) or replacing EDC's bespoke hydration with the generic path — a domain decision, not a code fix. That is the h7b handoff and is untouched here.

the_skew_that_IS_in_scope.method: Per-surface-form, per-fact counts over pokemon-lore's hydrated layer.
the_skew_that_IS_in_scope.interpretation: Uniform rendering ties a fact's surface count to how many templates happen to fit its predicate — a property of the template file, not of the domain. That is real utilization imbalance and it is exactly what SoG's controlled allocation addresses.

implementation.mechanism: Group renders by fact; derive quota = median renders per fact (from the corpus, not hardcoded); allocate facts in ASCENDING candidate-count order so the long tail claims its entities' budget first; for facts over quota keep the renders whose entity_ids are currently least-used. Deterministic — ties break on record text.
implementation.reference_cited_in_docstring: Source2Synth / SoG secondary sampling + controlled allocation
implementation.invariant: A fact at or below quota keeps everything — balancing never starves the tail further.
implementation.generic_synth: NOT changed. synth_records already allocates a flat n per triple, so per-triple allocation is uniform by construction; the 7.0x figure above is a fact_key grouping artifact (several triples share one fact), not an allocation defect. Balancing there would mean varying n per triple pre-generation, which changes provider spend and needs its own measured decision — deliberately not bundled in here.

measured_on_kanto.estimand: generic_expand template floor over pokemon-lore/kanto, regenerated from the same triples
measured_on_kanto.reading: 28% of surfaces dropped for a 7.7% loss in effective distinct forms — the culled renders were largely redundant, which is the point of allocating by utilization rather than uniformly. Kanto already passed the balance gate (0.77 < 1.0), so this is an improvement, not a fix.

red_green.corpus: synthetic two-faction: one popular faction at 20 surfaces/fact, one long tail at 2
red_green.control: test_before_the_change_the_corpus_is_skewed asserts the raw spread really is 10x, so a balanced result means something
cases: per-fact spread bounded by quota after balancing
long-tail facts never culled (all keep their 2)
quota is derived — 4x supply and 40x supply yield different quotas
entity utilization levelled: popular/rare ratio strictly decreases

deviations: The brief's stated target — EDC balance cov <= 1.0 via generic_expand/generic_synth — is not achievable, because EDC's hydrated layer contains zero surfaces from either generator. Reported with the surface_form census rather than attempted.
generic_synth was left unchanged: its per-triple allocation is already uniform, so the prescribed change there would alter provider spend without addressing a measured defect.

quota = median is aggressive (kanto quota=2, dropping 28% of the template floor). Recorded with its diversity cost measured rather than tuned to look better; a gentler derived bound is a follow-up if the diversity gate ever objects.

Kanto's hydrated layer on disk was NOT regenerated — the measurement recomputes the template floor in-memory from the same triples. Regenerating would overwrite a corpus other receipts point at, and the comparison does not need it.
